# Janasandhajātaka (Ja 468)

**ID:** Ja 468
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Janasandhajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Prince Janasandha
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja468

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Janasandhajātaka* (Ja 468) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection, rendered in English by Bhikkhu Sujato as *Prince Janasandha* [SuttaCentral]. The narrative opening relates that the Buddha told this story while staying at Jetavana for the admonition of the King of Kosala, who had neglected his royal duties and the dispensing of justice due to intoxication with royal power and sensual pleasures [SuttaCentral; Collins 1998; Fausböll 1887]. 

To instruct the king, the Buddha recounted the past life of the Bodhisatta as King Janasandha [Collins 1998; Anandajoti 2010]. In the verses, King Janasandha expounds the "ten things that should be done" (*dasa ṭhānāni*), enumerating ten courses of action that, when neglected earlier in life, lead to remorse in the future—such as failing to acquire wealth or neglecting duty [Anandajoti 2010]. Guided by this teaching, the populace fulfilled these duties and attained rebirth in heaven, with the Buddha subsequently revealing that he himself was King Janasandha in that past life [Fausböll 1887].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal Pali reuse: the verses of the text are shared with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (volume 4, edited by Fausböll) as well as the later anthology *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī* (matching §3.4–12.4) [DharmaNexus; Fausböll 1887]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments (§6.4–7.3) with passages in the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (別譯雜阿含經, T 100) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
